papers.title: EmbodiedBench: Comprehensive Benchmarking Multi-modal Large Language Models for Vision-Driven Embodied Agents
papers.benchmark: EB-ALFRED, EB-Habitat, EB-Navigation (AI2-THOR, 5 subsets x 60 = 300 episodes), EB-Manipulation
papers.gain: N/A. Baselines (ALFRED/Habitat/Nav/Manip): GPT-4o 56.3/59.0/57.7/28.9; Qwen2.5-VL-7B 4.7/14.3/20.3/9.6; InternVL3-8B 10.3/24.3/29.3/11.5. Without vision GPT-4o EB-Nav drops 57.7->17.4; an oracle single target box raises it 61.7->68.3.
papers.limitation: Error analysis covers only GPT-4o (10 failures per subset). EB-Nav subsets have 60 episodes, so one episode is 1.7 pp. No per-category failure breakdown for <=8B models.

papers.title: Embodied Agent Interface: Benchmarking LLMs for Embodied Decision Making
papers.gain: N/A. Llama-3-8B module average 28.4 (VirtualHome) / 23.1 (BEHAVIOR) vs GPT-4o 63.3/59.8. Missing step is the dominant runtime error (GPT-4o 15.1% / 36.0%).
papers.limitation: No visual input. The fine-grained error table covers only large models; Llama-3-8B appears only in the overview table.

papers.title: NavBench: Probing Multimodal Large Language Models for Embodied Navigation
papers.benchmark: 432 step-by-step VLN episodes in 72 Matterport3D scenes (gated) plus 3,200 QA pairs
papers.gain: N/A. Execution average: GPT-4o 41.33, Qwen2.5-VL-7B 21.77, Qwen2.5-VL-3B 13.00, InternVL2.5-8B 14.26, chance 8.19. MapGPT-style map text gives GPT-4o +4.86 SR on medium episodes.
papers.limitation: Uses gated Matterport3D and a discrete viewpoint graph. Error-type shares appear only in a figure (not extracted). Map test run only on GPT-4o.

papers.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
papers.venue_year: NeurIPS 2023 (from common citation; the arXiv page does not state it)
papers.benchmark: ALFWorld (134 text tasks), HotpotQA, HumanEval, WebShop
papers.gain: ALFWorld 130/134 tasks, +22% absolute over ReAct in 12 trials (GPT-3). ReAct alone plateaus at a 22% hallucination rate.
papers.limitation: Needs repeated trials on the same task. Self-reflection is 'an emergent quality of stronger, larger models' (starchat-beta gains nothing). Fails on exploration-heavy WebShop. With Qwen2.5-VL-72B on EmbodiedBench, Reflexion scores 38.3 vs BrainMem 75.0.

papers.title: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
papers.benchmark: Text agent tasks (the abstract lists none; commonly cited as ALFWorld, WebShop, HotpotQA, unverified)
papers.gain: The abstract reports consistent improvement as experience accumulates. Exact numbers not verified here.
papers.limitation: Text-only with API LLMs; insight quality depends on a strong model. None of the EmbodiedBench memory papers found here benchmark it.

papers.title: AutoManual: Constructing Instruction Manuals by LLM Agents via Interactive Environmental Learning
papers.gain: From one demonstration: 97.4% ALFWorld success with GPT-4-turbo, 86.2% with GPT-3.5-turbo. The manual can also guide smaller LLMs.
papers.limitation: Text environment with code-as-plan. Rules are built by strong API LLMs. No visual embodied evaluation.

papers.title: Agent Workflow Memory
papers.gain: +24.6% (Mind2Web) and +51.1% (WebArena) relative success. Online AWM gains +8.9 to +14.0 points under distribution gaps.
papers.limitation: Web domain only; workflows induced by strong LLMs; no embodied or visual evaluation.

papers.title: ELITE: Experiential Learning and Intent-Aware Transfer for Self-improving Embodied Agents
papers.gain: Online, unsupervised: Qwen2.5-VL-72B ALFRED 52->61, Habitat 59->63; InternVL3-78B 37->44 and 62->67. Supervised setting (training-split experience): ALFRED 49.8->70.8.
papers.limitation: Only 72B/78B backbones. Planner errors propagate into retrieval. Discrete household actions only.

papers.title: BrainMem: Brain-Inspired Evolving Memory for Embodied Agent Task Planning
papers.gain: GPT-4o: ALFRED 56.3->75.0, Nav 57.7->71.0, Manip 28.9->46.9, Habitat 59.0->63.3. With Qwen2.5-VL-72B: 75.0 vs RoboMemory 70.5, Voyager 46.5, Reflexion 38.3.
papers.limitation: Nothing below 72B tested. Guided retries on test tasks feed memory. About 1.4x more tokens. Long-horizon goal inference stays weak.

papers.title: PRACTICE: From Experience to Expertise in Self-Evolving Embodied Agents
papers.gain: Frozen Qwen3-VL-32B executor: ALFRED 24.3->49.7, Habitat 37.3->58.3. GPT-5.4: 65.3->67.7. Beats MemCompiler (40.0), LangMem, Mem0 and A-Mem.
papers.training_free: no (the Qwen3-VL-8B skill learner gets SFT plus on-policy distillation, about 71 GPU-h on 8xA100); the executor stays frozen
papers.limitation: Small gains for strong executors. ALFRED Long reaches only 24%. Still below ELITE and ORBIT on ALFRED. Some reported numbers are internally inconsistent.

papers.title: RoboMemory: A Brain-inspired Multi-memory Agentic Framework for Interactive Environmental Learning in Physical Embodied Systems
papers.gain: Qwen2.5-VL-72B: +26.5% average success over its baseline, beating Claude-3.5-Sonnet.
papers.limitation: 72B backbone with parallel multi-module overhead. No evidence for small models.

papers.title: EMHO: EMbodied Agent Harness Optimization via Experience Traces
papers.benchmark: EB-Navigation, EB-Manipulation (each split into search and held-out halves)
papers.gain: Held-out: Qwen3.5-9B Nav 48.7->56.7, Manip 10.7->21.0; 27B Nav 66.0->75.3, Manip 26.4->39.4. Removing experience traces drops Nav-Base 76.7->70.0.
papers.training_free: yes (model frozen; the same model edits its own harness over 10 iterations)
papers.limitation: Held-out scores are maxima over iterations, which is optimistic. No Reflexion, ExpeL or GEPA baselines. Overfitting acknowledged. A one-shot Opus revision nearly matches on 27B Nav. No cost report.

papers.title: Think Twice, Act Once: Verifier-Guided Action Selection For Embodied Agents (VeGAS)
papers.benchmark: Embodied reasoning benchmarks in Habitat and ALFRED (exact splits unverified)
papers.gain: Up to 36% relative gain over strong CoT baselines on the hardest multi-object, long-horizon tasks.
papers.training_free: no (verifier trained on an LLM-synthesized failure curriculum); policy frozen
papers.limitation: Key negative result: an off-the-shelf MLLM used as the verifier gives no improvement.

papers.title: RoboMonkey: Scaling Test-Time Sampling and Verification for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.benchmark: Simulated and real manipulation with VLAs
papers.gain: +25% absolute out-of-distribution, +9% in-distribution. Action error follows an exponentiated power law in the number of samples.
papers.training_free: no (VLM action verifier trained on synthetic data)
papers.limitation: Low-level VLA manipulation, not VLM planners or navigation. Many samples per step add latency.

papers.title: Limits and Gains of Test-Time Scaling in Vision-Language Reasoning
papers.gain: Closed models gain from structured reasoning and self-refinement. Open VLMs are inconsistent: external verification is the most reliable lever, iterative refinement often hurts, and perception-heavy tasks gain little.
papers.limitation: Not embodied, but a direct warning against self-refinement methods for small open VLMs.

papers.title: DIRECT: When and Where Should You Allocate Test-Time Compute in Embodied Planners?
papers.gain: The router matches or beats a stronger model's success at up to 65% lower average latency. CoT depth, model size and memory length each help different capabilities.
papers.limitation: Manipulation only, per-subtask routing. No EmbodiedBench or navigation results.

papers.title: MindJourney: Test-Time Scaling with World Models for Spatial Reasoning
papers.gain: Average +7.7% on SAT with no fine-tuning. Also improves RL-trained VLMs.
papers.limitation: A video-diffusion world model is heavy for an 8 GB GPU shared with a simulator. Static QA, not closed-loop control.

papers.title: Reflective Planning: Vision-Language Models for Multi-Stage Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation (ReflectVLM)
papers.gain: Beats commercial VLMs and MCTS-based post-training (exact numbers not verified).
papers.training_free: partly (the VLM is iteratively post-trained; reflection uses a generative dynamics model at test time)
papers.limitation: Manipulation-specific and needs a trained generative dynamics model.

papers.title: PIVOT: Iterative Visual Prompting Elicits Actionable Knowledge for VLMs
papers.benchmark: Real navigation and manipulation, simulated instruction following, localization
papers.gain: Zero-shot control with no robot data (qualitative). In VLMnav's HM3D ObjectNav comparison, PIVOT gets 24.6% SR vs 50.4% for VLMnav.
papers.limitation: The authors call it 'far from perfect'. Several VLM calls per step. Weaker than single-shot action projection for navigation.

papers.title: End-to-End Navigation with Vision Language Models: Transforming Spatial Reasoning into Question-Answering (VLMnav)
papers.gain: ObjectNav SR 50.4% vs 29.8% prompt-only and 24.6% PIVOT (Gemini Flash). Ground-truth depth gives 50.4 vs 39.1 with ZoeDepth.
papers.limitation: Only Gemini Flash tested. 13.9% of GOAT runs stop 1-1.5 m short. Ignores the robot footprint and has no backtracking. Naively concatenating history does not help.

papers.title: Set-of-Mark Prompting Unleashes Extraordinary Visual Grounding in GPT-4V
papers.gain: Zero-shot GPT-4V with SoM beats fully fine-tuned SOTA referring models on RefCOCOg.
papers.limitation: Built for GPT-4V. On EB-Navigation, multiple boxes hurt GPT-4o (53.3 vs 61.7 with none and 68.3 with an oracle single target box).

papers.title: SeeNav-Agent: Enhancing Vision-Language Navigation with Visual Prompt and Step-Level Policy Optimization
papers.category: visual prompting (BEV + front view) + step-level RFT
papers.gain: Zero-shot VP: GPT-4.1 65.0->86.7. VP+SRGPO: Qwen2.5-VL-3B 16.7->72.3 (GRPO 40.8, GiGPO 29.4).
papers.limitation: VP draws a target box and an agent-to-target line in both views, so it needs the target location. The source isn't stated and is probably simulator state. Only 60 tasks. No compute report.

papers.title: Neurosymbolic Embodied Agents
papers.gain: Open 4B-27B models exceed 90% in both environments. On ALFWorld, constraints or search alone solve under a third of tasks; combined they solve over 95%. The smallest agent beats a 27B direct visual policy.
papers.limitation: Needs a hand-written PDDL transition model. Correctness depends on visual grounding. High-level symbolic actions only.

papers.title: RPMS: Enhancing LLM-Based Embodied Planning through Rule-Augmented Memory Synergy
papers.category: action validity: rule retrieval + belief-gated memory
papers.gain: Llama-3.1-8B 59.7% (+23.9 pp, of which rules alone give +14.9 pp). Claude Sonnet 4.5 98.5% (+11.9).
papers.limitation: Text-only. Finds episodic memory harmful unless it is filtered by current state and explicit rules.

papers.title: Enabling Extensible Embodied Capabilities with Tools (Embodied Tool Protocol, EmbodiedToolBench)
papers.gain: Average +31% on EB-ALFRED and +36% on EB-Navigation. Qwen3-VL-8B ('Qwen3-8B' in the table): ALFRED 0.20->0.72, Nav 0.42->0.80. Nav Long gains +0.54.
papers.limitation: Nav tools give 'GPS-like guidance' (navigation_action_advisor, scene_graph), so privileged information is possible (unverified). ALFRED Long gains about 0.01. Qwen3-8B tool-result utilization is 0.04.

papers.title: ReDAct: Uncertainty-Aware Deferral for LLM Agents
papers.gain: Deferring about 15% of decisions to the large model matches using it for everything, at much lower cost.
papers.limitation: Text-only with no visual uncertainty. Not tested on EmbodiedBench or navigation.

papers.title: Sibyl: An Efficient Small-large Model Collaboration Framework for Long-horizon Tasks
papers.benchmark: ALFWorld and other long-horizon text tasks
papers.gain: From the prior sweep (agents.json, abstract tail not re-read): ALFWorld 95.2-97.4% with 0.3-0.8 cloud calls per episode and 21-44x lower API cost.
papers.training_free: no (three-stage RL; about 150-206 GPU-h on MI308X per the prior sweep)
papers.limitation: Text-only small models (Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B). Heavy RL. Needs a cloud model.

papers.title: SCALE: Self-uncertainty Conditioned Adaptive Looking and Execution for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.benchmark: Simulated and real VLA manipulation benchmarks
papers.gain: Improves SOTA VLAs and beats prior test-time scaling methods with a single forward pass (numbers not verified).
papers.limitation: Continuous-action VLAs, not VLM planners or navigation.

papers.title: Robots That Ask For Help: Uncertainty Alignment for Large Language Model Planners (KnowNo)
papers.venue_year: CoRL 2023 oral (CoRL not in CCF list)
papers.benchmark: Simulated and real-robot tasks with ambiguous instructions
papers.gain: Statistical task-success guarantees with minimal human help (exact numbers not verified).
papers.limitation: Needs multiple-choice option likelihoods. Escalates to a human, not to a stronger model.

papers.title: ERA: Transforming VLMs into Embodied Agents via Embodied Prior Learning and Online Reinforcement Learning
papers.gain: Qwen2.5-VL-3B: 0->65.2 on ALFRED and 0->48.3 on Manip, vs GPT-4o 56.8/28.9. Unseen splits: ALFRED 60.0, Manip 43.8.
papers.training_free: no (EPL on 2 H200 nodes for 2-5 h; RL on 2xH200 for about 12 h)
papers.limitation: No EB-Navigation or EB-Habitat results. RL from the base 3B model scores 0. Needs trajectories augmented by a stronger model.

papers.title: Embodied-Reasoner: Synergizing Visual Search, Reasoning, and Action for Embodied Interactive Tasks
papers.category: light fine-tuning (imitation + rejection sampling + reflection tuning)
papers.benchmark: AI2-THOR interactive search (809 tasks, 12 unseen scenes)
papers.gain: Qwen2-VL-7B 14.79->80.96% SR, beating o1 (71.73), Claude-3.7-thinking (67.70) and GPT-4o (66.67).
papers.training_free: no (9.39k synthesized trajectories; compute not reported)
papers.limitation: Uses its own task suite, so results are hard to compare. On the search subtask it trails o3-mini (65.16 vs 78.57) because it over-explores.

papers.title: World-aware Planning Narratives Enhance Large Vision-Language Model Planner (WAP)
papers.venue_year: arXiv 2506.21230, 2025 (a papers.nips.cc 2025 search hit suggests NeurIPS 2025; not opened)
papers.gain: Qwen2.5-VL: +60.7 absolute task success, with commonsense +60.0 and long-horizon +70.0. Beats GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.
papers.limitation: EB-ALFRED only. Data generation needs strong models. Compute not checked.

papers.title: RoboGPT-R1: Enhancing Robot Task Planning with Reinforcement Learning
papers.gain: Qwen2.5-VL-3B beats GPT-4o-mini by 21.33% and other Qwen2.5-VL-7B-based work by 20.33%.
papers.limitation: PRACTICE's table gives it 55.3 on ALFRED but only 22.0 on out-of-domain EB-Habitat, so transfer is weak.

papers.title: Embodied-R1: Reinforced Embodied Reasoning for General Robotic Manipulation
papers.benchmark: 11 embodied spatial and pointing benchmarks, SIMPLEREnv, 8 real XArm tasks
papers.gain: SOTA on 11 pointing benchmarks. 56.2% zero-shot on SIMPLEREnv and 87.5% on 8 real XArm tasks (+62% over baselines).
papers.training_free: no (3B VLM, two-stage RFT on Embodied-Points-200K)
papers.limitation: Manipulation-focused. No EmbodiedBench or navigation results found.

papers.title: On-Policy Reinforcement Fine-Tuning with Offline Reward for Multi-Step Embodied Planning (ORBIT)
papers.category: light fine-tuning (on-policy RFT with offline reward)
papers.gain: Claims SOTA on EB-ALFRED over closed-source and online-RL methods. PRACTICE reports 72.4 averaged over 5 splits (Long excluded).
papers.limitation: PRACTICE reports 22.4 on out-of-domain EB-Habitat. ORBIT's own tables were not read.

saturated: Experience, memory and skill libraries on EB-ALFRED and EB-Habitat with >=32B or API models: ELITE, BrainMem, RoboMemory, PRACTICE, WorldMind (2601.13247), MemCompiler, LangMem. GPT-4o with BrainMem already reaches 75.0 on ALFRED, so another memory scheme for large models would be incremental.

R1-style SFT+RL of 3B-7B VLMs on EB-ALFRED: ERA 65.2, ORBIT 72.4 (5 splits), ELITE-supervised 70.8, WAP +60.7, RoboGPT-R1, Reinforced Reasoner 41.6. These need multi-H200 compute and transfer poorly (about 22 on out-of-domain EB-Habitat). Not competitive on one 8 GB GPU.

Text or symbolic high-level planning: ALFWorld and VirtualHome success is at 95-98% (Embodied Planner-R1 97.78%, Neurosymbolic agents >95% with 4B-27B models, RPMS 98.5%, AutoManual 97.4%). Little headroom, and reviewers will treat it as solved.

EB-Navigation with tools or privileged visual prompts: ETP up to 0.85, SeeNav 86.7 (GPT-4.1), EMHO 75.3 (27B). New EB-Nav gains only mean something under a strict protocol with no privileged information.

Naive test-time scaling for open VLMs: self-refinement often hurts open VLMs (2512.11109), an off-the-shelf MLLM verifier gives no gain (VeGAS), majority voting lowers per-problem accuracy for 7-8B models on hard tasks (2608.11403), and consistency gains come mostly from decoding format (2608.01207).

Reflexion-style verbal self-reflection as the main contribution: it works mainly for strong models (Reflexion paper). With Qwen2.5-VL-72B on EmbodiedBench it scores 38.3, against 70-75 for newer memory systems.

Training-free zero-shot ObjectNav and VLN on HM3D/MP3D with frontier value maps or scene graphs (VLFM, SG-Nav, UniGoal, WMNav, CogNav, MSGNav, TrajRAG, RATE-Nav 67.8, fast-slow ReAct 68.75): crowded, and the scenes are gated anyway.
Learned small-to-large routing and escalation for text agents (ReDAct, Sibyl, TACIT-Switch 2608.27911, Bayesian self-escalation 2608.24087, DIRECT): theory and text-only versions already exist.
open_gaps: Training-free methods for <=8B local VLMs on EmbodiedBench. Every verified training-free gain uses >=9B (EMHO) or >=32B/API models (BrainMem, ELITE, PRACTICE, RoboMemory). Small baselines are weak: Qwen2.5-VL-7B 4.7 ALFRED / 20.3 Nav, InternVL3-8B 10.3 / 29.3, Qwen2.5-VL-3B 0 on ALFRED. A method here must not depend on the small model's own self-critique.

Geometric grounding without privileged information for low-level navigation. GPT-4o EB-Nav errors are 46% reasoning (23% spatial reasoning, 23% reflection) and 23% inaccurate action (overshoot). VLMnav stops 1-1.5 m short in 13.9% of GOAT runs, and EMHO agents pass the target 23% of the time. SeeNav and ETP may use simulator-derived target cues. Small-model cues from depth, odometry and detectors are open.

Free external verifiers for small VLMs. Off-the-shelf MLLM verifiers fail (VeGAS), and open VLMs gain only from external verification (2512.11109). This sweep found no work using environment validity feedback, depth-based collision checks, detector agreement or progress geometry as verifiers for best-of-N or lookahead on EmbodiedBench.

Long-horizon exploration for small models. EB-Nav Long scores 0.0 for Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL2.5-8B and 5.0 for InternVL3-8B (the target isn't visible at the start). ETP's largest Nav gain is on Long (+0.54) with scene-graph tools, which suggests explicit exploration memory helps. No training-free small-model method targets this.

Context and history representation for small models. Chat history helps GPT-4o (57.7 vs 45.3) but hurts Qwen2-VL-7B (14.0 vs 16.3 without) and Qwen2-VL-72B (21.2 vs 36.3), while InternVL2.5-8B collapses without it (21.3->5.7). ERA finds 1-step history plus a self-summary beats longer windows. A principled compact state for small models is still open.

Tool-output use by small models. In ETP, Qwen3-8B recognizes the need for a tool with 0.31 recall and uses tool results at 0.04, and missed tool calls cause 36% of EB-Nav errors. Injecting tool results straight into the prompt or action space, instead of relying on tool calls, is unexplored for small models.

Per-step escalation from a small to a larger VLM based on visual uncertainty on EmbodiedBench or AI2-THOR. Only text-only work (ReDAct, Sibyl) and per-subtask manipulation routing (DIRECT) turned up. Under the user's constraints the larger model must also run locally (e.g., a 2-4B default escalating to a quantized 7-8B), which limits the headroom.

Evaluation hygiene as a contribution. EB-Nav subsets have 60 episodes, EMHO reports maxima over iterations, BrainMem learns from guided retries on test tasks, and SeeNav and ETP may use privileged cues. No work offers a fixed-protocol, multi-seed evaluation with paired significance tests and no privileged information on ungated benchmarks.

Termination and progress estimation. Wrong termination is 13% of GPT-4o EB-ALFRED failures and rises to 29% after BrainMem. NavBench finds progress estimation weak for every model except GPT-4o, and RATE-Nav shows termination matters for ObjectNav. A calibrated stop-or-continue module for small models is open.

No published per-category failure breakdown for <=8B models on EB-Navigation or EB-ALFRED. EmbodiedBench, ERA and NavBench analyze GPT-4o or give only figures. A quantified failure taxonomy for small models could ground a method's motivation.
small_model_error_analysis: EB-ALFRED, GPT-4o (EmbodiedBench Fig. 6, 10 failures per subset): planning 55% (missing steps 23%, invalid actions 22%, inaccurate action 9%, action-ID mismatch 1%), reasoning 41% (reflection 17%, wrong termination 13%, insufficient exploration 12%), perception 4% (wrong recognition 3%).

EB-Manipulation, GPT-4o (EmbodiedBench Fig. 6): planning 44% (inaccurate action 42%, invalid action 1%), perception 33% (wrong recognition 22%, spatial understanding 8%, hallucination 4%), reasoning 23% (reflection 13%, spatial reasoning 10%).

EB-Navigation, GPT-4o (EmbodiedBench Fig. 17): reasoning 46% (spatial reasoning 23%, reflection 23%, insufficient exploration 1%), perception 31% (wrong recognition 22%, hallucination 4%, spatial understanding 4%), planning 23% (inaccurate action 23%, e.g., three steps instead of two). Hallucinating the target causes premature stops.

Small-model score profile (EmbodiedBench tables): Qwen2.5-VL-7B EB-Nav 20.3 with Long 0.0; InternVL2.5-8B Long 0.0; InternVL3-8B 29.3 with Long 5.0. EB-ALFRED: Qwen2.5-VL-7B 4.7, InternVL3-8B 10.3, InternVL2.5-8B 2.0. Qwen2.5-VL-3B scores 0 on ALFRED and Manipulation (ERA). EB-Nav base: Qwen2.5-VL-3B 16.7, 7B 20.0 (SeeNav).

History sensitivity on EB-Nav (with vs without chat history): GPT-4o 57.7 vs 45.3 (Long 55.0 vs 15.0); InternVL2.5-8B 21.3 vs 5.7; Qwen2-VL-7B 14.0 vs 16.3; Qwen2-VL-72B 21.2 vs 36.3. EmbodiedBench also reports that multi-step images confuse MLLMs about their current state.

Vision dependence: without images GPT-4o EB-Nav drops 57.7->17.4 (Long 0%), but language-only variants match or beat vision on high-level ALFRED and Habitat. So high-level failures are mainly planning and validity, while low-level navigation failures involve perception and spatial reasoning.

Visual overlays on EB-Nav: multiple detection boxes hurt (GPT-4o 53.3 multi vs 61.7 none; Claude-3.5 48.3 vs 46.7), while one oracle target box helps (68.3 and 58.3). Clutter hurts, and target localization is a bottleneck.

BrainMem, GPT-4o EB-ALFRED failures: with no memory (131 failures), invalid actions 20%, incorrect termination 19%, missing steps 19%, perception 5%. With memory (75 failures), incorrect termination rises to 29% and perception mismatch to 16%, so termination and perception become the leftover bottlenecks.

ETP tool-use errors on EmbodiedBench: missed tool invocation causes 36% of EB-Nav and 45% of EB-Manip errors; ignored tool output causes 47% (ALFRED) and 43% (Habitat). Tool-induced bias reaches 56.5% for Qwen3-VL-8B on Manip. Qwen3-8B recalls tool need at 0.31 and uses results at 0.04.

EMHO behavior statistics (Qwen3.5-27B, held-out, before -> after harness): navigation runs with >=5 consecutive rotations ~10% -> 3%; after explicitly identifying the target, arrival 43% -> 62% and passing the target 23% -> 7%; no-progress steps on visual-appearance tasks 35% -> 26%; valid next action after a blocked move ~44% -> 68%.

VLMnav (Gemini Flash): 13.9% of GOAT runs stop 1-1.5 m short (distance misjudgment). Estimated depth costs about 11 SR points vs ground truth (39.1 vs 50.4). Concatenating more history doesn't help (46.8 with none vs 40.4 with 15 steps). Without sliding on collisions, SR collapses 50.4 -> 12.9.

NavBench (Matterport3D, 100 failures): four types, namely incorrect plan, misaligned action, failure to stop (overshoot or early stop) and hallucinated movement. Percentages appear only in a figure and weren't extracted. Progress estimation is poor for every model except GPT-4o. InternVL2.5-2B/8B fall near chance on medium and hard episodes.

Embodied-Reasoner (AI2-THOR search): on composite tasks the repetitive exploration rate is 54% for o3-mini and 43% for Qwen2-VL-72B, vs 26% for the trained 7B explorer. Base Qwen2.5-VL-7B gets 12.38% SR and Qwen2-VL-7B 14.79%.

Embodied Agent Interface (symbolic): Llama-3-8B action-sequencing task SR is 21.3 (VirtualHome) and 10.0 (BEHAVIOR), vs GPT-4o 71.5 and 47.0. Missing step dominates runtime errors (GPT-4o 15.1% and 36.0%), and Llama-3-70B hallucinates objects or actions in 14.1% on VirtualHome.

Reflexion: a ReAct-only ALFWorld agent converges to a 22% hallucination rate, and self-reflection quality emerges only in larger models. GTR (ICCV 2025): outcome-only RL on a LLaVA-7B ALFWorld agent causes 'thought collapse' (less diverse, state-irrelevant reasoning and then invalid actions).

ERA error analysis (unseen ALFRED, 100 tasks; Manip, 98 tasks): the high-level task is dominated by reasoning and planning errors, the low-level task by perception and reasoning errors. EPL lowers every type, and RL mostly lowers reasoning and planning errors. Exact percentages appear only in Fig. 7 and weren't extracted.

Not found: no paper reports per-category failure percentages for <=8B VLMs on EB-Navigation or EB-ALFRED. Every quantified breakdown above is for GPT-4o or larger, or uses tool-use or behavior statistics.
verification_notes: All arXiv IDs, titles and arXiv comment or journal-ref venues were checked through the arXiv API. Numbers come from the fetched HTML or PDF text of EmbodiedBench, ERA, SeeNav, NavBench, EMHO, PRACTICE, BrainMem, ELITE, ETP, VLMnav, Reflexion and EAI. The EmbodiedBench pie charts were read from the PDF text layer.
Figure-only percentages were not extracted for ERA Fig. 7, NavBench Fig. 8 or SeeNav Fig. 1, because image rendering was unavailable.
Venues marked 'unverified' were not stated on the fetched pages. Sibyl's numbers come from the earlier agents.json sweep. ORBIT's numbers come from PRACTICE's table plus ORBIT's ACL abstract.
Whether SeeNav's VP target box and ETP's navigation advisor use simulator ground truth is inferred from their descriptions and is not confirmed.
